Mary Rocky Aged 55 Years W/O. Rocky, Residing At Thayyil House, Meykkad P.O., Angamaly, Ernakulam, Pin - 683589 2. VARGHESE SEBASTIAN AGED 70 YEARS S/o Sebastian RESIDING AT 207, MOOLAN HOUSE, KALLUPALAM NAGAR,ANGAMALY P.O., ERNAKULAM, PIN - 683572 3. MARGARET VARGHESE AGED 69 YEARS W/O. VARGHESE SEBASTIAN, RESIDING AT 207, MOOLAN HOUSE, KALLUPALAM NAGAR,ANGAMALY P.O., ERNAKULAM., PIN - 683572 4. VIJAY MOOLAN AGED 39 YEARS S/O. VARGHESE SEBASTIAN, RESIDING AT 207, MOOLAN HOUSE, KALLUPALAM NAGAR,ANGAMALY P.O., ERNAKULAM, PIN - 683572 RESPONDENTS/STATE/DEFACTO COMPLAINANT: 1. STATE OF KERALA REPRESENTED BY THE PUBLIC PROSECUTOR, HIGH COURT OF KERALA, ERNAKULAM, PIN - 682031 2. THE FOOD SAFETY OFFICER OFFICE OF THE FOOD SAFETY OFFICER, ANGAMALY CIRCLE, NAYATHODU P.O, ERNAKULAM, PIN - 683572 Application praying that in the circumstances stated therein the High Court be pleased to stay all further proceedings pursuant to A1- complaint and all further proceedings in ST.No.1357/2020 pending on the files Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Angamaly till the disposal of the above Crl.MC. This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application and upon hearing the arguments of M/S. MILLU DANDAPANI, RAMEEZ NOOH, Advocates for the petitioners,and PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the respondents, the court passed the following: p.t.o. Crl.MC No.3197/2023 2/4 Mary Rocky vs State Of Kerala on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70904816/ 1
texts.facts: Order The petitioners are accused Nos.1 to 4 in S.T.No.1357/2020 pending on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Angamaly. The case originated from the complaint of the 2nd respondent against petitioners 1 to 4 under Section 42(5) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("the FSS Act" for short) alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 26(1), 26(2)(i), 27, 59(i) and Section 3(1)(zz)(iii) and 3(1)(zz)(x) of the FSS Act. The allegations in the complaint are to the following effect; On 15.02.2020, at about 01:15 am, the Food Safety Officer, Angamaly Circle Vigilance Squad reached the premises 2025:KER:65144 of M/s.Moolans Exports (India) Pvt. Ltd., Angamaly, Ernakulam, in which the 1st petitioner is working as the Food Business Operator and the Sqaud purchased 2 kg of 'coriander whole' kept for sale along with other food articles for the purpose of analysis by issuing Form VA notice to the 1 st petitioner. Thereafter, sampling was done and a sample was sent in Form VI to the Food Analyst. After analysis Form VIIA report was submitted to the Designated Officer, Ernakulam as per which the sample contained Rodent Excreta (Contamination) which is injurious to health. Therefore, it was found that the food articles are unsafe as per 3(1)(zz)(iii) and 3(1)(zz)(x) of the FSS Act and that the sample doesn't conform to the standards of coriander under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Addictives) Regulations, 2011 and is therefore substandard as per Section 3.1(zx) of FSS Act. Petitioners 2 to 4, being the Directors of the said company, are also liable for the said offence as they have not submitted their nomination as per the FSS Act and thereby the accused persons 2025:KER:65144 have together committed the aforesaid offences.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would point out that in terms of the provisions of Section 42 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Food Analyst, after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer, is required to analyze the sample and send the analysis report mentioning methods of sampling within a period of 14 days to the designated officer with a copy to the Commissioner of Food Safety. It is further submitted that under Sub-Section 3 of Section 42, the designated officer, after scrutiny of the report of the Food Analyst, is to decide as to whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or fine only and in the case of contravention punishable with imprisonment he is required to submit recommendation within 14 days to the Commissioner of Food Safety for sanctioning the prosecution. The learned counsel submits that in the case on hand, the prosecution sanction order was issued from the office of the Commissioner of Food Safety only on 11.08.2020, though the report issued by the Food Analyst was on 05.03.2020. Reliance is placed on the order rendered by the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court to bolster his contention that the delay is fatal and the proceedings are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the complaint and further proceedings are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK], since the prosecution of the petitioners, in their alleged capacity as Directors of the Food Manufacturer, M/s.Moolans Exports (India) Private Limited, is an abuse of process, since the company is not made an accused. In support of the argument, reference is made to Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act dealing with vicarious liability of the Directors of the accused company and reliance is placed on the decision of the Apex Court in Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels and Tours Private Limited [(2012) 5 SCC 661]. Support for the argument is also sought to be drawn from the decision of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Maruti Prasad Panda v. State of Punjab [CRM-M No.18039 of 2024 dated 13.11.2024]. 3. It is submitted that in the case at hand, the report of the Food Analyst was issued as early as on 05.03.2020, but the Designated Officer had forwarded the request for sanction to 2025:KER:65144 initiate prosecution only on 11.08.2020. It is pointed out that as per Section 42(3) of the FSS Act, the Designated Officer, after scrutiny of the report of the Food Analyst, has to decide whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or only fine and in case the contravention is punishable with imprisonment, send recommendations within 14 days to the Commissioner of Food Mary Rocky vs State Of Kerala on 13 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177596435/ 3 In the FSS Act, offences by companies is dealt with in Section 66, extracted below; 2025:KER:65144 "66. Offences by companies.- (1) Where an offence under this Act which has been committed by a company, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that where a company has different establishments or branches or different units in any establishment or branch, the concerned Head or the person in-charge of such establishment, branch, unit nominated by the company as responsible for food safety shall be liable for contravention in respect of such establishment, branch or unit: Provided further that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act, if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. " 6. In Aneeta Hada (supra), after considering the vicarious liability of Directors of a company, with reference to Section 141 of the N.I.Act which is pari materia with Section 66 of the FSS Act, the Apex Court has held that for maintaining 2025:KER:65144 the prosecution, arraigning the company as an accused is imperative and the Directors cannot be prosecuted without the company being arrayed as an accused. In Maruti Prasad Panda (supra)the Punjab and Haryana High Court has held the prosecution under the FSS Act to be illegal without the company being arraigned as an accused.
